findings.severity_label: 📐 Maintainability & Code Quality | 🟡 Minor | ⚡ Quick win
findings.claim: Partial-progress tests depend on `chmod 0o444` actually blocking a write. Both copies force the sweep to throw by making the second migration read-only, which has no effect when tests run as UID 0 (common in CI containers) — the write succeeds, no error is thrown, and the test fails on its own guard instead of exercising the partial-result path.

findings.severity_label: 📐 Maintainability & Code Quality | 🟡 Minor | ⚡ Quick win
findings.claim: Close the clack session before exiting non-zero. Every other abort path in this function emits `if (!embedded) p.outro('Migration aborted.')` before `throw new CliExit(1)`; this new fail-closed exit doesn't, so a standalone run terminates without an outro.

findings.severity_label: 📐 Maintainability & Code Quality | 🟡 Minor | ⚡ Quick win
findings.claim: Duplicate warning with a dangling colon. `rewriteEncryptedMigrations` already emits the identical "…the rewrite left alone. Review them before migrating:" warning per directory followed by the actual statement list (Lines 198-206), and the same for unsweepable dirs (Lines 185-187).

Guard the partial-result read against non-object throws. `err as Partial<RewriteSweepError>` is an unchecked cast: for `throw null` / `throw undefined`, `partial.rewritten` raises a `TypeError` inside the catch and escapes `sweepMigrationDirs`, defeating the per-directory fail-closed reporting.

findings.severity_label: nitpick | 📐 Maintainability & Code Quality | 🔵 Trivial | 💤 Low value
findings.claim: Add the `"public"` rationale to both rewriters or centralize the assumption. `packages/wizard/src/lib/rewrite-migrations.ts` documents that `"public"."<domain>"` is an install-schema assumption, but `packages/cli/src/commands/db/rewrite-migrations.ts` emits the same unconditional qualifier with only a short comment.

findings.severity_label: nitpick | 🩺 Stability & Availability | 🔵 Trivial | ⚡ Quick win
findings.claim: Guard the partial-result carrier before reading it. A caught value may be `null`/`undefined`; this assertion does not change runtime behavior, so `partial.rewritten` can throw and mask the intended `CliExit(1)` path.
